findings.source_passage: Next morning Stubb accosted Flask. 'Such a queer dream, King-Post, I never had.'
findings.why_it_matters: The opening hook—'Such a queer dream, King-Post'—establishes Stubb's voice and his nickname for Flask ('King-Post') immediately; the draft converts it to indirect narration, losing the direct-speech register and the 'King-Post' address that characterizes their relationship.
findings.suggested_fix: Open with Stubb's direct speech: 'Such a queer dream, King-Post, I never had,' preserving the nickname and the sudden colloquial energy.

findings.source_passage: 'What am I about?' says I at last. 'And what business is that of yours, I should like to know, Mr. Humpback? Do you want a kick?'
findings.source_locator: middle of the dream narration, after 'slews me round'
findings.why_it_matters: This exchange—Stubb's defiant sass toward the merman, culminating in 'Do you want a kick?'—is the comic pivot of the dream and sets up the marlinspike reveal; its omission removes both the humor and the structural logic of what follows.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore Stubb's challenge to the merman ('Mr. Humpback? Do you want a kick?') and the marlinspike revelation so the dream's comic arc is intact.

findings.source_passage: his stern was stuck full of marlinspikes, with the points out. Says I, on second thoughts, 'I guess I won't kick you, old fellow.'
findings.source_locator: middle of the dream narration, after the merman bends over
findings.why_it_matters: The marlinspike image is the punchline of the dream's central joke—a vividly grotesque sight gag—and 'I guess I won't kick you, old fellow' is its deadpan payoff; both are entirely cut, gutting the comedy and the symbolic warning about consequences.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the marlinspike image and Stubb's 'I guess I won't kick you, old fellow' before the merman's 'Wise Stubb' repetition begins.

findings.source_passage: he all of a sudden seemed somehow, in some queer fashion, to swim off into the air. I snored; rolled over; and there I was in my hammock!
findings.why_it_matters: The triple-beat sentence 'I snored; rolled over; and there I was in my hammock!' is rhythmically distinctive and tonally funny—the abrupt bathos of waking; the draft's 'Stubb woke in his hammock' is a bare fact.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'I snored; rolled over; and there I was in my hammock!' verbatim as the wake-up line.

summary: No high-severity signature losses; three medium findings involve the erasure of 'King-Post,' the merman confrontation comedy, and the marlinspike punchline—significant voice flattenings but not individually regeneration-triggering, and they total exactly three medium findings, placing the verdict at the borderline; the draft preserves the chapter's core interpretive material (ivory-leg honor, pyramid, white whale warning) adequately.
